4. Place the title 'Choice of K - Neighborhood Size' centered horizontally inside the gray header band, in a large bold sans-serif font, colored dark red (#B00020).
5. Place the slide-number badge: a yellow (#FFF200) circle with a thin dark outline at the top-right corner (centered near ~95% width, ~8% height), containing the text '57' in dark text (body_text #000000).
6. Create the plot row: three equal-sized square charts placed side by side with small equal gaps, occupying ~10-90% width and ~40-80% height of the slide — left = K = 1, center = K = 3, right = K = 31.
7. Give all three plots identical axes: horizontal axis labeled 'x_6' (small italic math with subscript 6) with tick labels '0', '1', '2'; vertical axis labeled 'x_7' (small italic math with subscript 7) with tick labels '0', '1', '2'; feature space spans 0-2 by 0-2.
8. Place the caption 'K = 1' as small black math-style text directly above the left plot.
9. Place the caption 'K = 3' as small black math-style text directly above the center plot.
10. Place the caption 'K = 31' as small black math-style text directly above the right plot.
11. Fill the left (K = 1) plot with three semi-transparent decision regions — pink (#F4A6A6), light green (#B7F0B1), light periwinkle (#C9C9F2) — arranged in a highly fragmented, jagged pattern: periwinkle across the top, green on the right and lower areas, pink interleaved in the lower-left.
12. Fill the center (K = 3) plot with the same three region colors, with smoother, less jagged boundaries: periwinkle band across the top, large green region on the right, pink wedge in the lower-left/center.
13. Fill the right (K = 31) plot with the same three region colors, smoothest of all: periwinkle across the top, broad pink horizontal band through the middle, green region at the bottom (fine local detail washed out).
14. Overlay the training scatter on all three plots with small dots in red (#FF0000), green (#00CC00), and blue (#0000CC): blue cluster along the top (x_7 ~1.7-1.9), red cluster in the lower-left/center, green points scattered across the lower area.
15. Add exactly one small gray (#808080) hollow circle marker near coordinates (1.3, 1.6), inside the periwinkle region of the left (K = 1) plot only.
